newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Gasunie says may build Belgian gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Gasunie says may build Belgian gas pipeline.

text.p: Dutch gas distributor Nederlandse Gasunie said on Wednesday building a pipeline in Belgium was just one option it was considering to import gas from Britain.
"We have not yet made a decision. All options are still open," said Gasunie spokesman Pieter Bakker.

On Tuesday, the Flemish regional governments granted preliminary permission to Gasunie to build an underground pipeline between Zeebrugge and Ossendrecht at the Dutch/Belgian border. Assuming, the Belgian government agrees the plan, Gasunie will be free to construct the pipe.
Belgian Distrigas had hoped to retain its monopoly of gas distribution in Belgium.

The significance of the pipeline is that it would feed British gas imports directly into the Dutch network once the Interconnector pipeline from Bacton on Britain's east coast to Zeebrugge in Belgium is completed in October 1998.
Bakker said other options Gasunie was considering were a transport agreement with Distrigas or the construction of an offshore pipeline linking the Interconnector pipeline to Dutch coast.
However, cost appeared to weigh against the offshore option, he said.
Some commentators doubt that Gasunie seriously wishes to build a pipeline in Belgium.
"You can question whether they are doing this to have some leverage over Distrigas," said one industry observer.
Bakker said Gasunie will reach a decision early next year.
A Dutch regional supply company which plans to rival Gasunie's gas import business has said its imports of British gas will arrive via the Belgian network.

"We are working out some of the details, but (the gas) will come through Distrigas," said Leendert Florussa, project manager at Energie Zuid Nederland, a regional utility company in the southern Netherlands.
The Interconnector gas pipeline will bring up to 20 billion cubic metres a year of gas from the U.K. to continental Europe.
Gasunie is 50 percent owned by the Dutch state and 25 percent each by Royal Dutch/Shell and Exxon Corp unit Esso.
